row.evidence: Alteryx One help: "SCIM auto-provisioning is available only with the Enterprise Edition"; the pricing page lists Enterprise Edition as Contact Sales above Starter at $250 USD per user/month billed annually.
row.notes: Alteryx One editions: Starter $250/user/mo annual (1-10 seats, cloud only), Professional and Enterprise Contact Sales; Enterprise starts at 10+ users. SCIM 2.0 with a workspace tenant URL and admin-generated bearer token (lifetime in days); requires SAML SSO on the workspace first. Okta's OIN Alteryx One app is SAML only, so Okta and Entra use the generic endpoint per Alteryx's guides. Deprovisioning disables the user and removes roles; disabled users still count against the workspace limit. SSO tier is not stated on the pricing page or docs. Self-hosted Alteryx Server has separate Entra SCIM and a v3 user API.

scim.base_url: Workspace-specific Tenant URL shown in Admin Console > User Provisioning (pattern not published)

auth.token_source: Workspace Admin Console > User Provisioning > Automatic User Provisioning > Alteryx Token Authentication > Generate Token
auth.token_expiry: Lifetime set in days at generation (setup guides use 365)

endpoints.notes: Endpoint paths are not listed; Users and Groups are implied by the documented user provisioning and Push Groups against the tenant URL.

operations.notes: Okta guide enables Create Users, Update User Attributes, Deactivate Users and Push Groups. Removing a pushed group deletes the matching Alteryx user group.

deprovision.data_retained: User is disabled and roles removed; a disabled user's assets remain but ownership does not transfer (admin has ownership privileges). Disabled users still count against the workspace limit.

attributes.notes: Attributes are the ones the Okta and Entra guides tell admins to keep; Okta matches users on email.

roles.how: IdP security groups become Alteryx user groups; roles are assigned to those user groups in Admin Console and inherited by members.

limitations.text: SAML SSO must be enabled on the workspace before SCIM (Okta and Entra guides).
SCIM overrides manual user and group changes made by workspace admins.
SCIM-originated changes carry originating_service CUSTOMER_SCIM in audit events.

scim.notes: Researched for Alteryx One (cloud). Self-hosted Alteryx Server has its own SCIM integration with Microsoft Entra ID, which needs SAML SSO on the Server.

capabilities.notes: Alteryx One help says the API can invite and revoke access for batches of users; the full reference (api-docs.us1.alteryxcloud.com) is a JS app that did not load. Alteryx Server API v3 separately supports create, list, get, update, deactivate and delete users.

endpoints.purpose: Invite a batch of users to a workspace (Alteryx One)
Alteryx Server: transfer a user's assets

audit_log_api.notes: Audit Logs page offers CSV download; Enterprise adds scheduled Audit Log Export to customer storage. No audit-log API endpoint found.

limitations.text: Alteryx Server API v3 user endpoints apply to self-hosted Alteryx Server (part of Enterprise Edition), not the Alteryx One cloud workspace.

okta.notes: OIN Alteryx One app marks SAML only; Alteryx's guide turns on 'Enable SCIM provisioning' on the workspace's app and enters the generic tenant URL and token.

entra.notes: Gallery tutorial covers Alteryx Server SSO; Alteryx One SCIM is configured on an existing enterprise app with the tenant URL and secret token.

google.notes: Alteryx documents Google Cloud Platform OIDC SSO; no Google provisioning documented.

open_questions: Which edition includes SAML/OIDC SSO is not stated on the pricing page or in the docs read.
SCIM endpoint paths, PUT vs PATCH, delete support, filtering and pagination are not documented in the public setup guides.
Lowest edition with API access is unclear: the Starter admin guide has an OAuth clients page, while API Access is listed as a Professional/Enterprise capability.
Full Alteryx One API reference (users, groups, roles endpoints, rate limits) sits on api-docs.us1.alteryxcloud.com, which could not be rendered.
Whether SCIM deactivation ends active sessions is not documented.
